answer: Simplest version: each submission is re-executed by 3 peers drawn at random and their outputs must match. When peers disagree the credit is diluted by one third per dissent rather than split, so a wrong answer earns 0. Quorum must span 2 unrelated subnetworks, which means a farm hosting everything in one datacenter cannot fill its own panel. A copy costs the same as the original and earns 0. The garden grows only where 3 strangers agree, and the fable of a self-graded pearl ends at the second subnet.
